boundary_evidence.boundary: Platform authorization BEFORE key access and privileged client construction
boundary_evidence.evidence: The action freshly checks getUser and get_staff_context, then preflights. The factory repeats that fresh guard before reading SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY. The independently passing revocation test instruments process.env and asserts zero privileged-key reads. The factory is server-only, creates a distinct supabase-js client with persistence/auto-refresh/URL detection disabled, and forwards no caller cookies, storage or user session. Configuration errors use fixed safe strings; raw construction/provider errors are not returned. A fresh browser build scan found no private key canary, private variable name or factory name in any of 19 static files.

boundary_evidence.boundary: Course/organization/tournament binding and atomic, non-escalating data writes
boundary_evidence.evidence: The server rejects submitted org/role/user/redirect fields and validates bounded UUID selections. SQL derives the organization from the active course, locks selected event rows in UUID order and validates exact course/org and active state again during completion. New membership uses staff; conflicts do nothing. Only explicitly selected revoked grants are re-enabled; active grants retain original attribution, existing owner/admin roles and other grants remain untouched. Ordinary, owner, anonymous and revoked callers are denied. Actual PGlite tests forced a failure after an earlier selected grant and read back rollback of membership, grants and their audit rows while retaining the Auth identity. Zero selections add no event grants. Existing catalog/event-creation membership semantics are unchanged, not misrepresented as a new all-event grant.

boundary_evidence.boundary: Definer privileges, RLS, search_path and unchanged preexisting authorization
boundary_evidence.evidence: Both public RPCs reach the platform-guarded private scope helper, use security definer with empty search_path and qualified application objects, revoke PUBLIC/anon execution and grant only authenticated execution. The private helper is not client executable. Completion uses the caller-authenticated RPC, not service-role writes, so audit actor auth.uid() remains the real caller. An additional independent in-memory PGlite before/after catalog comparison confirmed every preexisting policy, relation ACL, function definition and function ACL unchanged. Catalog readback confirmed all three new functions are definers with search_path="", no PUBLIC/anon execute, and authenticated execute only on the two public RPCs. This is real SQL/catalog evidence under synthetic Auth fixtures, not deployed-inventory proof.

boundary_evidence.boundary: Existing identity reuse, duplicates and safe partial failure/retry
boundary_evidence.evidence: SQL resolves the existing account by case-insensitive exact email rather than accepting a user ID. Existing-account default path does not construct the privileged client or reset password/metadata; explicit resend uses only inviteUserByEmail(email,{redirectTo}). Duplicate-email error codes proceed to fresh exact-email DB completion. Errors distinguish known accepted invitation requests from uncertain Auth progress, sanitize provider messages and advise reviewed retry without deleting identities/memberships. Grants and membership are one DB transaction, not falsely described as atomic with Auth/email. Transport-double success proves application branching only; actual provider duplicate/resend behavior remains RG2.

boundary_evidence.boundary: Invitation/callback/password semantics, fixed redirects and secret non-disclosure
boundary_evidence.evidence: The landing rejects extra/repeated parameters and unintended types; GET never verifies a token. An explicit action POST validates type=invite and hash shape and calls verifyOtp, then redirects only to /auth/set-password. The password view and action freshly call getUser; the action accepts only matching 12-128 character passwords and updates only password before fixed /admin redirect. Existing password login is unchanged. The configured invitation origin rejects credentials/path/query/fragment and non-HTTPS except exact supported local development hosts. Added production code contains no password/token/invite-link/key/provider-exception logging or sensitive result-state echo. HTTP checks independently witnessed no-referrer/no-store/noindex controls on invitation responses. External access-log redaction remains RG6.

l1_disposition.independent_evidence: After an independent fresh production build, node --test verification/staff-session-refresh.test.mjs exited 0: all 4 tests passed, none failed/skipped. Both expired and nearly expired password-page requests refreshed exactly once, rendered with the replacement session and returned replacement access AND refresh cookies. A subsequent HTTP POST using the actual rendered React bound-action fields and those persisted cookies returned 303 to /admin; the fake Auth listener observed exactly one password update with the replacement bearer and no additional refresh. The /login persistence control passed; invitation GET/HEAD/prefetch made zero Auth calls and set no session cookies. This independently verifies the bounded lost-cookie defect is corrected; it does not prove real Auth rotation or browser acceptance.

primary_source_comparison.assessment: Installed SDK source explicitly says admin invitations do not support PKCE; inviteUserByEmail sends the email and redirect without a verifier. Token-hash verifyOtp supports invite, persists the returned session and emits SIGNED_IN. Password update uses the current session bearer, saves the user and emits USER_UPDATED. The application uses these actual interfaces rather than an invented PKCE/fragment callback.

Server Component writes are prohibited; proxy must forward refreshed request and response cookies before rendering. The exact password-route matcher now supplies that path without running Auth on the invitation landing. Installed Next docs also state action POSTs use their hosting route and require independent authorization inside the action.

Cached official material supports server-only administration, exact redirect allowlists, authenticated updateUser password setup, custom TokenHash/RedirectTo invite links for SSR, and deliberate confirmation to mitigate link prefetch. The handoff template matches this architecture. Missing secrets/template/SMTP settings and real browser/provider behavior are deployment/acceptance gates, not proof supplied by mocks. No hosted documentation or service request was made during this review.
